title: Cue-card prototypes + brittle cases
content:
Purpose / context:
This is my fast scratchpad for cue-card style prompts (short, repeatable templates) and a compact catalog of brittle failure cases to test in the prompt library harness. Goal is to create tiny templates that an engineer can copy into a Redwood API call and run quick A/Bs, plus keep a running list of weird failure modes we keep hitting in production QA and sandboxing.

Notes to self (voicey):
- Keep shots tiny: 2–4 examples max for client-facing short templates.
- Prefer explicit constraints over trusting temperature to behave.
- When testing, always try: system-only, system+one-shot, system+few-shot, and system+chain-of-thought-off.
- Record top-3 failure symptoms (consistency, hallucination, instruction-ignoring).

Quick cue-card templates (copyable):
1) Summarize-for-engineer (short):
System: "You are a concise engineering summarizer. Output plain text, bullets, no code blocks."
User: "Summarize the following issue for an engineer: {{ISSUE_TEXT}}"
Example behavior: short bullets, one-line root cause guess, next-action suggestion.

2) User-intent-to-action (bounded):
System: "You are an assistant that maps user intent into a single actionable command. Output only a JSON object with fields: action, confidence (0-1), params."
User: "User says: '{{USER_UTTERANCE}}'"
Post-process: if parsing fails return {"action":"unknown","confidence":0.0,"params":{}}

3) Quick-fact-check (source tag):
System: "Verify whether the factual claim is supported by the provided source. Answer: SUPPORTED / CONTRADICTED / INSUFFICIENT. Give 1-sentence justification and a source-quote if available."
User: "Claim: '{{CLAIM}}'\nSource: '{{SOURCE_SNIPPET}}'"

Few-shot set (compact, for intent classification):
- Shot 1: Input: "How do I reset my API key?" -> Output: "intent: account_management, intent_detail: api_key_rotate"
- Shot 2: Input: "We're seeing 503s from the endpoint" -> Output: "intent: incident, intent_detail: infra_503"
- Shot 3: Input: "Can I get better latency if I batch requests?" -> Output: "intent: optimization, intent_detail: batching_query"

Negative / fragile examples (explicit):
- Long, multi-step user prompts where the real intent is buried in the middle: model tends to paraphrase but miss the intended action.
- Overlapping named entities: 'Redwood' as company vs 'redwood' as tree in examples — causes wrong grounding.
- Ambiguous dates: "this quarter" without context -> model invents current quarter boundaries.
- Hallucinated citations: when asked to cite line numbers or logs, model fabricates a plausible but nonexistent log line.

Brittle cases catalog (test IDs for harness):
CASE-B1: Intent inversion on negations
Trigger: Input like "I don't want the summary to include opinion" -> Model appends opinionated take anyway.
Test: Force explicit avoid phrases and check for presence of opinion adjectives.

CASE-B2: Token-overlap bleed in few-shot sets
Trigger: Few-shot examples share unique token sequences that appear in the new input -> new output copies example tokens verbatim when not appropriate.
Mitigation: shuffle few-shot order, use paraphrasing, or remove exact shared tokens.

CASE-B3: Prefix cache poisoning (runtime)
Trigger: prefix cache optimization introduces stale context across rapid variants -> reuse artifacts from previous prompt.
Check: run same template with different USER_UTTERANCE quickly, assert independent outputs.

CASE-B4: Numeric-literal regression
Trigger: multi-step math where intermediate rounding varies -> final answer format inconsistent.
Test: enforce 'round to 2 decimal places' in system; if not followed, mark failure.

Guided experiments to run in harness (short):
- Temperature sweep: 0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.9; capture BLEU/ROUGE vs ground truth for summarization tasks.
- Prompt order test: shot order A/B with same set -> measure stability (KL on token distribution or exact match rate).
- System prompt ablation: remove system line and compare instruction-following score.
- Model variant fallback: compare responses across r-inference/light-quant vs r-inference/standard-hosted to surface quantization-caused hallucinations.

Checklist for each run:
- seed id 
- model + variant 
- prompt template id (e.g., cue-ENG-SUM-001)
- few-shot ids used 
- temp + top_p + max_tokens 
- test_case ids invoked (from brittle catalog)
- metrics logged: exact_match, contains_forbidden_tokens, hallucination_flag, latency_ms

Example failure writeup (copy to bug ticket):
Title: "Model ignores explicit 'no opinion' constraint in engineer-summarizer template"
Repro steps:
1) Use template Summarize-for-engineer (see top).
2) Input: long postmortem with clear 'do not include opinion' line.
3) Run on model r-inference/standard-hosted at temp 0.2.
Observed: output includes two opinionated sentences ("I think...", "seems likely...").
Expected: zero opinion adjectives, only facts and next-action.
Attached: prompt JSON, model response, API request id: abc-xyz-123.
Suggested mitigations tried: tightened system prompt to "never speculate" (reduced but did not eliminate), added hard post-filter to strip adjectives (worked but brittle).

Open todos (short):
- Formalize cue-card id scheme (prefix cue- + TEAM + 3-digit).
- Add automatic heuristics runner that flags 'opinion words' via a lexicon and writes to ML-qa dashboard. (JIRA-9876)
- Try instruction-finetune regime with 10 targeted examples to reduce 'no-opinion' failures.

Random micro-notes:
- Try swapping 'Output only JSON' -> sometimes increases literal hallucination of field names; add validator.
- For fact-checking, include explicit source span anchors (e.g., line 3–7) to reduce INSUFFICIENT responses.
- When doing few-shot for classification, prefer canonicalized labels (snake_case) to avoid label synonyms in outputs.

Quick copy-ready Redwood API example (pseudocode):
POST /v1/responses
{ "model":"r-inference/standard-hosted", "input": "<system + user combined per cue>", "temperature":0.2, "max_tokens":256 }
Note: always include metadata: prompt_id, run_id, harness_case.

Historical context / why this doc exists:
I keep hitting small but recurring prompt bugs during partner POCs. This sheet is a compressed personal labbook so I can quickly repro and attach to tickets or PRs. Might convert to a small shared 'cue-card' repo if others find useful.

If you want to steal/use: copy the templates and run them through the harness. Ping me in #prompt-lab with the run id if you want me to triage.

----
Scratch log (short trails):
2026-01-08: observed opinions slip in 2/5 runs on Summarize-for-engineer.
2026-02-14: found prefix-cache reproduction with live autoscaling test.
2026-02-28: attempted JSON-output-only, saw fabricated field 'confidence_level' in 3/10 runs (model inventing).

End of doc.
